motivation: Qwen3-14B passed the full-profile capability gate at 12/12 under the documented Qwen3 reasoning/sampling configuration in v0.4. Run the official full multi-agent task to establish a local natural-discussion reference before testing structured protocols.

model.name: Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M
model.runtime: llama.cpp b11202; RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8 GB; 24 GPU layers with CPU offload; one slot; context 8192

design.retry_policy: The upstream client retries failed API requests up to three times; invalid vote responses can trigger up to three vote-level attempts, each with client retries. 408 is the planned number of successful responses, not a hard cap. Count actual requests, completions, and retries from the server logs.
design.persistence: Run one task per upstream CLI process with its official per-task seed; persist every task output before starting the next; merge only when all task outputs for a profile exist.

primary_outcomes: Full and hidden profile initial average and majority accuracy
Full and hidden profile final average and majority accuracy
discussion wire tokens and UTF-8 bytes
server prompt-evaluation tokens, generated tokens, requests, summed service latency, max context seen, and truncation count
analysis: Use the official HiddenBench scorer. Report per-task and both average/majority rules. Full vs hidden is a task/profile diagnostic. This three-task, one-model, one-seed study is not sufficient evidence for a general protocol claim or scaling law. This release compares no message formats.
limits: Only three related verification tasks and one run per profile.
Local Q4 model with partial CPU offload; latency is hardware-specific.
Prompt-evaluation token counts reflect llama.cpp cache-aware work and may undercount full client prompt tokens.
The full study is expensive; actual inference cost will be reported rather than inferred from the wire-token count.
